headline: High: unstructured can read/write files and egress allowlisted network, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk when paired with taipy's data-engineering outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Taipy has no documented shared channel or I/O surface, while unstructured reads documents and can write files. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not default, but if taipy outputs are manually copied into unstructured inputs or a shared workspace is introduced, file content could be treated as instructions. Uncertainty remains because taipy's I/O surfaces are empty.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies taipy-generated text into unstructured's document inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file-based instruction smuggling becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep taipy and unstructured on separate directories.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs and inputs.
Use read-only mounts for taipy artifacts.
Add a content-sanitization step before unstructured ingests taipy output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Taipy is docs-only with no network egress, but unstructured can read filesystem, process documents/images/text, and egress to allowlisted network endpoints. If both touch the same workspace, taipy-produced artifacts can be ingested and transmitted by unstructured. The pairwise leakage path exists in common setups, though taipy itself does not expose sensitive data handling.
conditions: IF taipy writes artifacts containing sensitive data into a workspace readable by unstructured, leakage is possible.
IF unstructured is configured to process those files, their contents can flow to allowlisted external services.
mitigations: Store taipy outputs in a private directory.
Restrict unstructured to a separate input folder.
Block network egress for unstructured during sensitive runs.
Redact sensitive fields before document processing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Taipy is a data-engineering tool and unstructured can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and support multiple instances. Even without explicit locks, overlapping writes to shared artifacts or pipelines can race. Taipy's lack of documented concurrency details adds uncertainty, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or pipeline state, file clobbering can occur.
IF taipy orchestrates jobs that unstructured also mutates, race conditions become plausible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts.
Use immutable filenames per run.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Taipy can generate data-engineering outputs that unstructured may consume as document inputs. Because unstructured processes files and text, taipy errors or malformed outputs can propagate downstream if treated as authoritative. There is no documented verification step in either profile, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests taipy-produced files without validation, taipy mistakes can cascade.
IF downstream automation trusts unstructured's parsed output, errors can amplify into later steps.
mitigations: Validate taipy outputs before ingestion.
Add schema checks on intermediate files.
Require human review for high-impact outputs.
Log and quarantine parse failures.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. Taipy has no touched data classes and no network egress, while unstructured handles documents/images/text and may call external docs/privacy endpoints. The only concrete compliance concern is that document data could be processed externally if configured, but the pairwise evidence is limited.
conditions: IF regulated documents are fed into unstructured and external API calls are enabled, compliance review is needed.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to those documents, the processing path must be checked.
mitigations: Classify document data before processing.
Disable external API calls for regulated data.
Confirm retention settings in unstructured.
Keep regulated workloads in a segregated environment.
